summary.headline: Fedbank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 52.5% YoY to ₹114.4 Cr, ROE crossed 15% at 15.4%, while GNPA fell to 1.6% after write-offs.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed AUM up 34.7% YoY to ₹21,136 Cr and PPOP up 50% YoY to ₹187.5 Cr, with direct assignment income turning negative at ₹13 Cr. Gold loan AUM grew 77% YoY to ₹11,191 Cr despite a roughly 15% fall in domestic gold prices and new RBI LTV rules effective April 1. Stage II rose from 2.2% to 2.7% due to the shift to periodic interest-due structures, which management attributes to customer re-adjustment rather than asset quality. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20-25% entity growth, 20-30 bps ROA expansion and sub-1% credit cost, and announced leadership changes in the LAP and gold businesses.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM ₹11,191 Cr (+77% YoY, +8.1% QoQ) with tonnage up ~1% QoQ; AUM per branch ₹17.7 Cr. Management says gold AUM can grow 25-30% in FY27 even with flat prices, mainly via tonnage (10-12% historical).

segments.name: Mortgage / LAP (overall)
segments.commentary: Mortgage AUM ₹9,777 Cr (+14-15% YoY), disbursements ₹673 Cr (+4% YoY). Management guides LAP (small + medium ticket) growth of 15-20% in FY27.

segments.name: Small ticket LAP
segments.commentary: Yield about 16%, ticket size ₹7-35 lakh; approval rates dropped, yield held. Jagadeesh Rao now heads it alongside gold and home loans; ~200 branches distribute it.

segments.name: Medium ticket LAP
segments.commentary: Ticket size ₹35 lakh-3 crore, yield about 12-12.5%; facing sharp competitive yield pressure, company not matching competitors yet.

guidance_outlook: Entity AUM growth about 20-25% in FY27 (about 20-22% in a later answer); gold AUM 25-30% growth on March 2026 base even with flat prices, mortgage 15-20%.
Credit cost to stay below 1% for FY27 (regular credit cost ~0.7%, Q1 about 0.8% including write-offs).
ROA to expand 20-30 bps over FY26 average of ~2.4%, via credit cost and cost-to-average-assets levers.
Add about 200 branches in FY27 (150 added in FY26); identified premises, Q1 openings slipped to Q2.
Expects leverage to de-lever over next few quarters as CLM co-lending normalises; FCNRB flows expected in Q2; CLM/DA partnerships to drive incremental growth to conserve capital.
Gold 1+ DPD optically 200-300 bps higher at entity level; management says new delinquency metrics are not comparable.
capex_capacity: Net 200 branch additions planned for FY27; Q1 saw none opened though premises were identified and work done.
AUM per branch ₹17.7 Cr; opex-to-assets reduction creates space to invest in new branches while sustaining ROA.
Expansion focus includes Odisha and northern territories with existing presence in ~18 states.
Operating costs expected to rise with originations as sourcing-related expenses scale.
demand_pricing: Gold prices fell about 15% between Jan 31 and Jun 30, 2026, a headwind to gold AUM; company lends on lower of 30-day average or spot price.

New RBI LTV rule from April 1 applies to bullet loans on total maturity amount; company moved to periodic interest-due structures, with quarterly and monthly products driving skew toward ticket sizes above ₹2.5 lakh.
Medium ticket LAP faces sharp yield competition; company is maximising yield and has not matched competitor pricing, leading to lower disbursements.
Small ticket LAP disbursements weaker on lower approval rates; yield not cut.
Auctions in Q1 were under ₹1 crore, per management.
Bank vs NBFC competition in income-generating loans described as unchanged; Fedfina also offers IGL.

qa_highlights.question: How has the company positioned itself under the new LTV rules, and how does competition with banks look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most gold lenders are moving to quarterly products that create dues, with optical impact on 1+ and 30+ DPD but no real asset-risk increase; Fedfina also offers IGL, so bank-NBFC competition is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Gold growth outlook if prices stay flat, and the role of income-generating loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 25-30% gold AUM growth even with flat prices, driven by 10-12% tonnage growth, with LTV expansion possible on quarterly and half-yearly products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did disbursements grow only 15-20% YoY when gold prices rose 30-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said disbursements translated to AUM growth at about the historical rate; Jagadeesh Rao said ticket sizes above ₹2.5 lakh skewed higher after the new regime, with no impact on high-ticket acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP growth and yields change, and what are the medium and small ticket LAP plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium ticket LAP yields are under pressure (about 12-12.5%), while small ticket LAP (about 16% yield) saw lower approval rates; management guided LAP growth of 15-20% and said it would reassess in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why were no branches opened in Q1 and is the 200-branch target intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premises were identified and work done but openings slipped; the 200-branch FY27 guidance is unchanged, with spillover into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Q1 provision and write-off figures and the FVOCI reclassification affect P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said write-offs were a little above ₹50 Cr, cutting GNPA by 30 bps, and the FVOCI-to-amortised cost reclassification caused ECL derecognition and re-recognition; DA loss reflects unwinding of past DA income exceeding new DA income.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in mortgage Stage 3 and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said collections were significantly scaled up; cases with property and limited enforceability (SARFAESI) are slow, and the company is pursuing legal, technical and field resolution over a longer period.

risks_watch: Gold delinquencies and reported 1+/30+ DPD under the periodic interest-due structure; management expects elevated overdue levels near term.
Medium ticket LAP yield compression and small ticket LAP approval rates could keep disbursements below guidance.
Leverage at 4.89x and CRAR down to 20.71%; de-leveraging depends on CLM co-lending normalising.
Mortgage Stage 3 rising QoQ and YoY with long recovery timelines; monsoon and West Asia impact flagged as Q2/Q3 uncertainties.
Branch openings (200 in FY27) back-loaded into Q2 onward; cost increases with originations.
Gold price volatility: lower prices raise LTV on AUM (67.9%).
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, growth and guidance, with management repeatedly saying all FY27 guidance is unchanged. More cautious and somewhat defensive on asset quality optics (1+ DPD, PCR, Stage II) and on LAP disbursements, where it blamed approval-rate and yield choices and promised to revisit in Q2/Q3.
